architecture.name: fa2-sm75-via-bridge-feasibility
architecture.head_dims: FlashAttention-2's Ampere path covers head_dim 32-256 (fwd and bwd instantiate 32/64/96/128/160/192/224/256; API accepts multiples of 8 and pads to multiples of 32 via d_rounded). The working Turing port (ssiu/flash-attention-turing) covers head_dim 64 and 128 only, fp16. The bridge-header design target (unmodified FA2 on sm_75 for baseline comparison) is therefore the full 32-256 forward set, with d=256 being smem-marginal on Turing (see d256_feasibility).
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: Not supported and not supported by a bridge: FA2's csrc carries a single kHeadDim template parameter that drives Q/K/V layouts identically (SmemLayoutQ, SmemLayoutKV, SmemLayoutVtransposed all reuse the same atom in csrc/flash_attn/src/kernel_traits.h); qk_dim == v_dim is assumed everywhere. No MLA 576/512 or partial-RoPE divergence handling exists; adding it would be kernel surgery outside the bridge-header goal.
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: GQA/MQA is supported natively and cheaply in both upstream FA2 and the ssiu Turing port via the h/h_k integer ratio (params.h_h_k_ratio), broadcasting K/V heads with no extra template axis or layout change. A bridge inherits this for free.
architecture.hybrid_pattern: Not applicable: FA2 is a full-softmax-attention kernel only; there is no linear-attention or gated-delta layer pattern. Feature surface is causal/local/sliding-window masks, softcap, dropout, ALiBi, varlen, append-KV and split-KV decode. The ssiu Turing port supports causal+non-causal, varlen and GQA; it omits dropout, local mask and KV cache.
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: No per-layer heterogeneous head-dim mechanism: head_dim is a fixed per-call template instantiation (8 static .cu files per dtype/causality/pass, generated by csrc/flash_attn/src/generate_kernels.py). Mixed-dim models need separate calls; the API-level padding path (d_rounded) is the only flexibility.

kernel_support.supported_dims: Upstream FA2 (master, verified 2026-09-06): head_dim in {32,64,96,128,160,192,224,256} for fwd, bwd and splitkv, fp16+bf16, via static per-hdim instantiation files (flash_fwd_hdim*_sm80.cu family) emitted by generate_kernels.py; runtime accepts head_size % 8 == 0 and pads to a multiple of 32 (d_rounded). Mechanism is pure template instantiation, no autotune. ssiu/flash-attention-turing: fp16 only, head_dim 64 and 128, causal/non-causal, fwd+bwd, GQA, varlen; dropout, local mask and KV cache not supported. Achieved on Turing by hand-tuned kernel_traits: SM75_16x8x8_F32F16F16F32_TN mma atoms tiled 8-warp Tile<128,32,8>, native ldmatrix LDSM atoms (SM75_U32x2/U32x4_LDSM_N, SM75_U16x8/U16x4_LDSM_T), and AutoVectorizingCopyWithAssumedAlignment<128> register-staged gmem->smem copies.
kernel_support.capability_gate: The real dependency map of FA2's Ampere path (csrc/flash_attn/src/kernel_traits.h, Flash_kernel_traits) is smaller than folklore: (1) MMA: SM80_16x8x16_F32F16F16F32_TN / SM80_16x8x16_F32BF16BF16F32_TN under __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800, with an #else fallback to SM75_16x8x8_F32F16F16F32_TN (Turing-native m16n8k8) that is ALREADY in master - the m16n8k16-to-2xm16n8k8 decomposition is pre-implemented, and utils.h convert_layout_acc_Aregs handles both K=8 (identity) and K=16 via if constexpr. (2) smem reads: SM75_U32x4_LDSM_N / SM75_U16x8_LDSM_T ldmatrix atoms under __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 750 - ldmatrix is native on sm_75, nothing to substitute. (3) gmem->smem: SM80_CP_ASYNC_CACHEGLOBAL<uint128_t> (cp.async.cg, 16B) only when Has_cp_async (>=800); the #else branch is AutoVectorizingCopyWithAssumedAlignment<128>, i.e. ld.global.v4->register->st.shared.v4 register staging - also already coded. (4) Pipelines: the sm80 path uses NO cutlass pipeline classes, no TMA, no mbarrier - just cute::cp_async_fence() / cp_async_wait<N>() + __syncthreads(); in CUTLASS's include/cute/arch/copy_sm80.hpp both are wrapped in CUTE_ARCH_CP_ASYNC_SM80_ENABLED (defined only when __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800) and compile to no-ops below sm_80, so the code compiles but degenerates to fully synchronous loads [uncertain: compile+run behavior of the <800 path has never been demonstrated end-to-end]. (5) bf16 is the only hard architectural absence: no bf16 tensor-core mma on sm_75, cuda_bf16.h and relu2<bfloat16_t> are SM80-guarded, and Flash_kernel_traits forces Element=cutlass::half_t below 800. Gates that actually block Turing today: flash_api.cpp has is_sm8x_min = cc_major >= 8 with TORCH_CHECK(..., "FlashAttention only supports Ampere GPUs or newer.") in all 5 entry points, and setup.py's FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS default is "80;90;100;110;120" with no sm_75 branch (setting 75 yields only a compute_75 PTX blob, no sm_75 SASS). Maintainer-stated blockers: exactly one - tridao in issue #1342 (2025-02-20): "The main challenge is that Turing does not have cp.async to load from global mem to shared mem" and "you'd need to change the memory loading (and change the synchronization pattern)"; everywhere else he cites only lack of bandwidth/contributors. There is no formal blocker list; the only list-like content is folkloric (bf16 absence, 64KB smem, CI effort), and the expected finding holds: the blockers must be derived from code, and the code already contains most of the substitution.
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: On Turing, stock FA2 fails hard, not silently: TORCH_CHECK(cc_major >= 8) raises "FlashAttention only supports Ampere GPUs or newer." in mha_fwd, mha_varlen_fwd, mha_bwd, mha_varlen_bwd and mha_fwd_kvcache. There is no fallback path inside the package. The ecosystem fallback is PyTorch SDPA, which on Turing dispatches to xformers' Memory-Efficient Attention (cutlassF, CUTLASS sm70+ kernel) per ssiu's README and xformers issue #950. If compiled below 800 with the current kernel_traits, behavior degrades silently in perf (no-op cp.async fences => zero load/compute overlap) rather than in correctness [uncertain: correctness of the never-shipped <800 path is inferred from code reading, every cp_async_wait is followed by __syncthreads and all copies become synchronous, but nothing has been validated on hardware].
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: sm_75 appears nowhere in FA2's build or test surface: setup.py emits gencodes only for 80/90/100/110/120, and GitHub-hosted CI jobs are build-only (no GPU); GPU tests run on self-hosted Ampere/Hopper/Blackwell-class machines [uncertain: exact runner inventory not exhaustively verified]. No claim of Turing support has ever been CI-exercised; ssiu's Turing port has no CI at all - it is validated by test_flash_attn.py runs on a T4 with CUDA 12.4 and PyTorch 2.5.1/2.8.0 (manual). Rotted-claim check: the old README line "Support for Turing GPUs (T4, RTX 2080) is coming soon. Please use FlashAttention 1.x for Turing GPUs for now" (quoted verbatim in issue #720, Dec 2023) has been replaced in current main by a pointer to ssiu/flash-attention-turing "which supports a core subset of FlashAttention features on Turing" - i.e. upstream has now outsourced Turing to the community port rather than delivering it.

performance.turing_baseline: Same-hardware numbers exist only from the ssiu port, on T4 (cc 7.5, 65 TFLOPS fp16 TC peak): initial state (issue #1533 body, 2025-03-12, head_dim=128, batch=4, heads=32, seq%128==0, no masking): ~2x faster than PyTorch F.scaled_dot_product_attention (Memory-Efficient/cutlassF backend) at ~63% compute throughput for long sequences. Current repo README (verified 2026-09-06): forward up to 2.19x (non-causal) / 1.95x (causal) vs PyTorch attention with up to 66% compute throughput; backward up to 1.35x (non-causal) / 1.51x (causal) with dK/dV kernels at 49% and dQ at 45% compute throughput. Baseline on Turing = cutlassF because PyTorch SDPA falls back to xformers Memory-Efficient Attention on sm_75 (xformers #950: cutlass backend 'a bit slower than Flash-Attention, but ... supports any GPU above P100'). Unverified claims to not rely on: AutoWHEELx2's ChatGPT-generated porting plan in #1342 claiming 2.1x / 72 TFLOPS on RTX 2080 Ti (mixed reactions, no artifacts). Historical anchor: FA1.x ran natively on Turing (FA2 README pre-2025 told Turing users to use FA 1.x); issue #542/#1235 document the community demand (T4 Kaggle competitions, TITAN RTX).
performance.d256_feasibility: Forward d=256 on Turing is smem-marginal but arithmetically possible; backward d=256 is infeasible. FA2's fwd launch template for d=256 uses kBlockM=128, kBlockN=64, kNWarps=8, Share_Q_K_smem=true, so kSmemSize = max(kSmemQSize, kSmemKVSize) = max(128*256*2B, 2*64*256*2B) = exactly 65536 B. Turing (cc 7.5) caps shared memory at 64 KB/SM and 64 KB/block, so this lands exactly at the limit - cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 65536) should accept it [uncertain: not compiled/run], leaving occupancy at one 256-thread block per SM. Register budget is the second wall: acc_o alone is 128*256/(8 warps*32 lanes) = 128 fp32 registers/thread, plus Q fragment, softmax state and pipeline registers, risking >255 reg/thread spill on sm_75 [uncertain]. Backward d=256 needs roughly triple-buffered Q/dO plus K/V/dS/dP smem (kSmemSize formula in Flash_bwd_kernel_traits), far above 64 KB - no way to fit on Turing without redesigning block sizes. ssiu's port deliberately stops at d=64/128; FA1 (which ran on Turing) supported head dims up to 256 including d=256 [uncertain: from search-result summary of current FA2 README, not independently verified]. For the bridge's purpose (baseline comparison), d<=128 (and possibly 96/160/192 with smaller kBlockN instantiations [uncertain]) is the realistic Turing coverage; d=224/256 baselines should be taken from cutlassF or emulation on Ampere instead.
performance.cost_analysis: Bridge-header cost breakdown (goal: run FA2 unmodified on sm_75): (1) Code substitutions actually required inside kernels: none by design - kernel_traits.h's #else branches already select SM75_16x8x8 mma (m16n8k8; the m16n8k16 tile becomes 2x the k-atoms, same MAC count, same fp32 accumulation semantics, instruction count doubles and per-instruction operand reuse halves), native LDSM ldmatrix atoms, and register-staged gmem copies; cute's cp_async_fence/cp_async_wait no-op below 800. (2) Host-side work: patch the cc_major >= 8 TORCH_CHECK in 5 entry points of flash_api.cpp, and add a sm_75 gencode branch (setup.py currently ignores 75 except as PTX-only compute_75 for forward-compat) - or vendor the csrc with FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS-style env hacking plus a one-line gencode patch. (3) The performance cost is the pipeline: with cp.async fences as no-ops, every load is ld.global->reg->st.shared and synchronous; the interleaving that hides ~50% of gmem latency on Ampere vanishes. ssiu demonstrates the fix costs a kernel rewrite: single smem buffer (V aliases K), next-K register prefetch into tKrK, and two __syncthreads() per iteration, reaching 63-66% compute throughput vs a naive synchronous pipeline expected materially lower [uncertain: no side-by-side measurement of no-op-fence FA2 exists]. (4) Smem/register budgets: fwd d=128 sm80-style tiles (e.g. kBlockM=128, kBlockN=128, Share_Q_K_smem) need 64KB - exactly Turing's per-block cap; Turing-viable configs must shrink kBlockN (ssiu uses its own 16x64 swizzle atoms and 128x32x8 mma tiles). (5) fp16-only: Element is forced to half_t below 800, so no bf16 branch is compiled. (6) Compile time: compiling the full fp16 fwd+splitkv (and bwd) per-hdim .cu set for one arch is the same order as one arch of the current build (~tens of template instantiations) [uncertain: not measured].

design_fit.route: C (bridge-header completeness for unmodified FA2), with ssiu's port as the reference implementation that route A/B-style rewrites are benchmarked against.
design_fit.recommendation: Do not write a from-scratch bridge header for the substitutions - upstream csrc already contains them (SM75_16x8x8 mma fallback, >=750 ldmatrix atoms, register-staged gmem copy selected when Has_cp_async=false, no-op cp.async fences). The concrete bridge work is host-side and small: (a) allow cc_major == 7.5 past the five TORCH_CHECK gates in flash_api.cpp, (b) build the fp16 _sm80.cu instantiations with arch=compute_75,code=sm_75 gencode, (c) restrict to fp16 (bf16 is structurally impossible on sm_75), (d) validate numerics on T4 against eager/SDPA because the <800 path has never shipped. For performance parity use ssiu/flash-attention-turing (now officially linked from the FA2 README) rather than the degenerate no-op-fence build; treat unmodified-FA2-on-Turing purely as the baseline-comparison instrument it is, expecting it to sit below ssiu's 2.19x/66%-throughput numbers due to fully serialized loads. Next actions: fork FA2, patch the gate + gencode, compile fwd hdim 64/128 fp16 first, run test correctness on T4, then measure against ssiu and cutlassF.
design_fit.numerics_risks: Low but nonzero. (1) Precision: fp32 accumulation throughout (ElementAccum=float, online softmax in fp32, exp2f scaling by log2(e)) - identical on sm_75; no bf16 involved since the Turing path is fp16-only by construction (Flash_kernel_traits forces half_t below 800). (2) The m16n8k8-for-m16n8k16 decomposition accumulates two sequential k=8 MMA results into the same fp32 accumulator - semantically the same order an m16n8k16 HMMA internally uses, so no reordering risk [uncertain: reasoning, not bit-level verified]. (3) Wrong-output history: no documented wrong-output bugs attach to the <800 branches (never shipped); the known FA2 wrong-output incidents concern other features. (4) The real risk is untested-code risk: zero-overlap pipeline with no-op fences relies on every cp_async_wait being paired with __syncthreads - a race would be a silent correctness bug, so hardware validation is mandatory. (5) Softcap/dropout paths reuse the same fp32 math and are fine; Turing has no bf16 so softcap in fp16 carries the usual fp16 dynamic-range caution.
design_fit.demand_weighting: Large installed base concentrated in exactly the head shapes the port covers: T4 is one of the most-deployed cloud/inference GPUs (Kaggle free tier, AWS g4dn, Colab), plus TITAN RTX/RTX 2080Ti owners (22GB 2080Ti mods cited in #787). Demand evidence: #720 has 38 thumbs-up, #542 18, #787 16/3; drivers are Kaggle competitions (LLM Science Exam, $1M AIMO per suicao's #542 comment) and Mistral/LLaMA models whose serving stacks require the flash_attn 2.x API (issue #1235: varlen + pad/unpad helpers only exist in 2.x). Head-shape distribution favors d=128 (most open LLMs) and d=64 (GQA-heavy smaller models) - exactly ssiu's coverage set; d=256 demand on Turing is negligible (d=256 models are Hopper-class workloads). Benefit accrues to inference-only users first (tridao's 2023-10-04 question in #542 - 'Is the usage on T4 just inference (forward pass only)?' - shows even the maintainer scoped the port around forward), with backward now also delivered by ssiu.
